# 1 Kings Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Now King David was old and advanced in years, and they covered him with garments, but he could not get warm.
**2** So his servants said to him, "Let a young woman, a virgin, be sought for my lord the king, and let her stand before the king and be his attendant. Let her lie in your bosom, that my lord the king may be warm."
**3** So they sought for a beautiful young woman throughout all the territory of Israel and found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
**4** The young woman was exceedingly beautiful, and she became the king's attendant and served him, but the king did not know her.
**5** Now Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, "I will be king." And he prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
**6** And his father had never at any time displeased him by asking, "Why have you done thus?" He was also very handsome in appearance, and his mother had borne him after Absalom.
**7** He conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they followed and helped Adonijah.
**8** But Zadok the priest and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada and Nathan the prophet and Shimei and Rei and David's mighty men were not with Adonijah.
**9** Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened calves by the Stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants.
**10** But Nathan the prophet and Benaiah and the mighty men and Solomon his brother he did not invite.
**11** Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, "Have you not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know it?
**12** Now therefore come, let me counsel you, that you may save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
**13** Go in at once to King David and say to him, 'Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your servant, saying, "Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'
**14** Then while you are still speaking there with the king, I also will come in after you and confirm your words."
**15** So Bathsheba went to the king in his chamber. Now the king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was attending to the king.
**16** Bathsheba bowed and prostrated herself before the king. And the king said, "What do you desire?"
**17** She said to him, "My lord, you swore by the LORD your God to your servant, saying, 'Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.'
**18** And now, behold, Adonijah is king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.
**19** He has sacrificed cattle, fattened calves, and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the sons of the king, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army. But Solomon your servant he has not invited.
**20** And now, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you, to tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
**21** Otherwise, when my lord the king lies down with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be counted as offenders."
**22** While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
**23** And they told the king, "Here is Nathan the prophet." And when he came before the king, he bowed before the king with his face to the ground.
**24** And Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you said, 'Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne'?
**25** For he has gone down this day and has sacrificed cattle, fattened calves, and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. And there they are, eating and drinking before him, and saying, 'Long live King Adonijah!'
**26** But me — your servant — and Zadok the priest and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada and Solomon your servant he has not invited.
**27** Has this thing been brought about by my lord the king, and you have not told your servant who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"
**28** Then King David answered and said, "Call Bathsheba to me." And she came before the king and stood before the king.
**29** And the king swore and said, "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my soul from every distress,
**30** as I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel, saying, 'Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place,' so will I do this day."
**31** Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and prostrated herself before the king and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"
**32** King David said, "Call to me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada." And they came before the king.
**33** And the king said to them, "Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
**34** And let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there as king over Israel. Then blow the trumpet and say, 'Long live King Solomon!'
**35** You shall then come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne, for he shall be king in my place. And I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and over Judah."
**36** And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king and said, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, so declare it.
**37** As the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David."
**38** So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites went down and caused Solomon to ride on King David's mule and brought him to Gihon.
**39** There Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. Then they blew the trumpet, and all the people said, "Long live King Solomon!"
**40** And all the people went up after him, playing on flutes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth was split by their sound.
**41** Adonijah and all his guests heard it as they finished feasting. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, "What is this uproar in the city?"
**42** While he was still speaking, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came. And Adonijah said, "Come in, for you are a worthy man and bring good news."
**43** Jonathan answered Adonijah, "No, for our lord King David has made Solomon king.
**44** The king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and they have caused him to ride on the king's mule.
**45** And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon, and they have gone up from there rejoicing, so that the city is in an uproar. This is the noise that you heard.
**46** Solomon now sits on the royal throne.
**47** Moreover, the king's servants came to bless our lord King David, saying, 'May your God make the name of Solomon more famous than yours, and make his throne greater than your throne.' And the king bowed himself on the bed.
**48** And the king also said, 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has granted someone to sit on my throne this day, my own eyes seeing it.'"
**49** Then all the guests of Adonijah trembled and rose, and each went his own way.
**50** And Adonijah feared Solomon. He arose and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.
**51** Then it was told Solomon, "Behold, Adonijah fears King Solomon, for behold, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, 'Let King Solomon swear to me first that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"
**52** And Solomon said, "If he proves to be a worthy man, not one of his hairs shall fall to the ground, but if wickedness is found in him, he shall die."
**53** So King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and bowed before King Solomon. And Solomon said to him, "Go to your house."

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA has reviewed the translations of EMET (literal), LOGOS (formal), and PNEUMA (dynamic) for this chapter.

**Method**: Each verse was compared across all three translations. The LOGOS formal translation serves as the primary consensus baseline, with adjustments where EMET's literalism reveals important Hebrew features or PNEUMA's dynamic rendering better captures the original intent.

**Key Observations**:
- EMET preserves Hebrew word order and particles (ʾet, vav-consecutive) that reveal syntactic emphasis
- LOGOS provides the most balanced English rendering suitable for study
- PNEUMA's dynamic approach often captures emotional register and narrative pacing most effectively

## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

**Chapter 1**: 34 verse(s) with significant divergence

### Verse 1
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Now King David was old and advanced in years, and they covered him with garments, but he could not get warm.
- **PNEUMA**: King David was now very old. No matter how many blankets they piled on him, he could not stay warm.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 2
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: So his servants said to him, "Let a young woman, a virgin, be sought for my lord the king, and let her stand before the king and be his attendant. Let her lie in your bosom, that my lord the king may ...
- **PNEUMA**: His servants said, "Let us find a young virgin to attend the king. She can lie beside you and keep you warm, my lord."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 4
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: The young woman was exceedingly beautiful, and she became the king's attendant and served him, but the king did not know her.
- **PNEUMA**: She was stunningly beautiful. She became the king's attendant and cared for him, but the king was not intimate with her.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 5
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Now Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, "I will be king." And he prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
- **PNEUMA**: Meanwhile, Adonijah son of Haggith began promoting himself, declaring, "I will be king!" He acquired chariots, horses, and fifty men to run ahead of him.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 6
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And his father had never at any time displeased him by asking, "Why have you done thus?" He was also very handsome in appearance, and his mother had borne him after Absalom.
- **PNEUMA**: His father had never once challenged him by asking, "What do you think you're doing?" Adonijah was also very handsome, and he was born next after Absalom.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 7
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: He conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they followed and helped Adonijah.
- **PNEUMA**: He conspired with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they threw their support behind him.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 9
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened calves by the Stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants.
- **PNEUMA**: Adonijah held a great sacrificial feast — sheep, cattle, and fattened calves — at the Stone of Zoheleth near En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's other sons, and all the royal officials o...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 11
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, "Have you not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know it?
- **PNEUMA**: Nathan went to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and asked, "Haven't you heard? Adonijah son of Haggith has made himself king — and David doesn't even know!
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 12
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Now therefore come, let me counsel you, that you may save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
- **PNEUMA**: Let me advise you how to save your life and the life of your son Solomon.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 13
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Go in at once to King David and say to him, 'Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your servant, saying, "Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah...
- **PNEUMA**: Go immediately to King David and say, 'My lord the king, didn't you swear to me that my son Solomon would succeed you and sit on your throne? Why then has Adonijah become king?'
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 14
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Then while you are still speaking there with the king, I also will come in after you and confirm your words."
- **PNEUMA**: While you're still talking with the king, I'll come in and back up everything you've said."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 16
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Bathsheba bowed and prostrated herself before the king. And the king said, "What do you desire?"
- **PNEUMA**: Bathsheba bowed low before the king. He asked, "What is it?"
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 18
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And now, behold, Adonijah is king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.
- **PNEUMA**: But now Adonijah has become king — and you, my lord, don't even know about it!
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 20
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And now, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you, to tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
- **PNEUMA**: My lord the king, all Israel is watching you, waiting for you to announce who will succeed you on the throne.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 21
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Otherwise, when my lord the king lies down with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be counted as offenders."
- **PNEUMA**: If you don't act, the moment you die, Solomon and I will be treated as criminals."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 22
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
- **PNEUMA**: While she was still speaking, Nathan the prophet arrived.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 23
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And they told the king, "Here is Nathan the prophet." And when he came before the king, he bowed before the king with his face to the ground.
- **PNEUMA**: They announced to the king, "Nathan the prophet is here." Nathan came before the king and bowed facedown.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 24
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you said, 'Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne'?
- **PNEUMA**: Nathan said, "My lord the king, did you declare that Adonijah would succeed you and sit on your throne?
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 27
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Has this thing been brought about by my lord the king, and you have not told your servant who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"
- **PNEUMA**: Has my lord the king authorized this without telling your servants who should sit on the throne after you?"
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 29
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And the king swore and said, "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my soul from every distress,
- **PNEUMA**: The king swore an oath: "As surely as the LORD lives — the God who has rescued me from every danger —
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 31
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and prostrated herself before the king and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"
- **PNEUMA**: Bathsheba bowed facedown and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 33
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And the king said to them, "Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
- **PNEUMA**: the king told them, "Take my personal guard, put my son Solomon on my own royal mule, and escort him down to Gihon.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 35
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: You shall then come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne, for he shall be king in my place. And I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and over Judah."
- **PNEUMA**: Then escort him back up, and he will take his seat on my throne. He will reign in my place, for I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 40
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And all the people went up after him, playing on flutes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth was split by their sound.
- **PNEUMA**: The whole crowd followed him back up, playing flutes and celebrating with such tremendous joy that the ground shook with the noise.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 41
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Adonijah and all his guests heard it as they finished feasting. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, "What is this uproar in the city?"
- **PNEUMA**: Adonijah and all his guests heard the commotion just as they were finishing their feast. When Joab heard the trumpet, he demanded, "What's all that noise from the city?"
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 45
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon, and they have gone up from there rejoicing, so that the city is in an uproar. This is the noise that you heard.
- **PNEUMA**: Zadok and Nathan anointed him king at Gihon, and they've come back up celebrating. The whole city is in an uproar — that's the noise you've been hearing.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 46
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Solomon now sits on the royal throne.
- **PNEUMA**: What's more, Solomon is already sitting on the royal throne.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 47
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Moreover, the king's servants came to bless our lord King David, saying, 'May your God make the name of Solomon more famous than yours, and make his throne greater than your throne.' And the king bowe...
- **PNEUMA**: The king's officials have even come to congratulate King David, saying, 'May God make Solomon's name even more famous than yours and his throne even greater!' The king bowed in worship from his bed.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 48
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And the king also said, 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has granted someone to sit on my throne this day, my own eyes seeing it.'"
- **PNEUMA**: David himself said, 'Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, who has let me see with my own eyes a successor on my throne today.'"
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 49
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Then all the guests of Adonijah trembled and rose, and each went his own way.
- **PNEUMA**: At this, all of Adonijah's guests panicked. They got up and scattered, each going his own way.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 50
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And Adonijah feared Solomon. He arose and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.
- **PNEUMA**: Adonijah himself was terrified of Solomon. He rushed to the altar and grabbed hold of its horns.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 51
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: Then it was told Solomon, "Behold, Adonijah fears King Solomon, for behold, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, 'Let King Solomon swear to me first that he will not put his servant to...
- **PNEUMA**: Solomon was told, "Adonijah is afraid of you and is clinging to the horns of the altar. He says, 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he won't execute his servant.'"
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 52
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: And Solomon said, "If he proves to be a worthy man, not one of his hairs shall fall to the ground, but if wickedness is found in him, he shall die."
- **PNEUMA**: Solomon replied, "If he proves to be loyal, not a hair on his head will be touched. But if he is found to be disloyal, he will die."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 53
- **EMET**: 
- **LOGOS**: So King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and bowed before King Solomon. And Solomon said to him, "Go to your house."
- **PNEUMA**: King Solomon sent men to bring Adonijah down from the altar. Adonijah came and bowed before King Solomon. Solomon told him, "Go home."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

— SOPHIA
